title: Sterilizing immune clearance of established metastatic carcinomas

concept.text: Proposed innovation: a controllable immune treatment that eliminates established, bulky carcinomas and their growing metastases while preserving essential normal tissues. Carcinomas arise from epithelial tissues; the intended scope includes difficult metastatic diseases such as pancreatic, microsatellite-stable colorectal, prostate, and hormone-receptor-positive breast cancer. The desired outcome is lasting clearance after treatment ends, rather than continued dependence on therapy to suppress tumor growth.

The central capability is coordinated immune rejection across heterogeneous tumor deposits: immune cells must reach the lesions, function within hostile tissue, and eliminate malignant populations despite differences among cells and sites. The supplied Nature Reviews Immunology abstract documents obstacles to solid-tumor CAR-T therapy involving trafficking, infiltration, immune suppression, and metabolic competition. CAR-T is an important route toward this goal, but the proposed innovation is defined by the therapeutic outcome rather than a particular immune platform.

Conceptual boundary: “sterilizing” expresses the ambition to leave no viable malignant population capable of regrowth. A clinical complete response, even one lasting years without treatment, cannot by itself establish that every malignant cell has disappeared. ONC-02 centers on established macroscopic disease and growing metastases; eliminating dormant disseminated reservoirs remains a closely related objective with its own biological and measurement problems.

significance.text: Conditional significance: if a treatment produced durable, treatment-free complete clearance in a majority of representative patients with these metastatic carcinomas, it would establish a major new therapeutic capability. The direct consequence would be reliable immune rejection of established disseminated carcinoma in the populations actually tested. It could reduce dependence on repeated treatment and prolonged disease suppression, provided toxicity, durability, and access were acceptable.

The clinical burden is illustrated by Mani and colleagues’ 2024 study, which reported a median survival of 10 months among patients newly diagnosed with metastatic cancer in a historical US SEER cohort covering 1992–2019. This pooled estimate describes that cohort; it is neither a contemporary prognosis for every metastatic cancer nor a measure specific to the proposed target carcinomas. It supplies context for the importance of metastatic disease without establishing how much any future treatment would improve survival.

Conditional limits: multiyear complete responses would support durable clinical remission, but declaring the diseases usually curable would require longer follow-up and evidence addressing late relapse. Antigen escape, residual malignant clones, and dormant reservoirs could undermine apparent clearance. Broad efficacy would also not automatically make treatment immediately available or affordable. Comparisons with immune-responsive cancers can motivate the ambition, but success in one cancer or selected subgroup does not establish equivalent susceptibility across common metastatic carcinomas.

missing_breakthrough.text: The target capability requires immune cells to enter and remain effective throughout substantial tumor masses and multiple metastatic sites. The retained Nature Reviews Immunology abstract describes impaired trafficking and infiltration, abnormal tumor vasculature, and dense extracellular matrix as obstacles. These barriers mean that generating tumor-reactive cells is only part of the problem: those cells must reach malignant tissue in sufficient numbers and maintain useful activity there.

Within the tumor, the same abstract identifies regulatory T cells, myeloid-derived suppressor cells, tumor-associated macrophages, checkpoint-mediated inhibition, and metabolic competition as constraints on immune function and persistence. The engineering challenge is to overcome several interacting resistance mechanisms while keeping the response controllable. The retained material supports these mechanisms, but does not establish that any single intervention resolves them together at clinically sufficient breadth.

Additional candidate barriers from the research are antigen heterogeneity, antigen loss, and injury to normal organs that share the targeted antigen. They frame an important recognition-and-safety problem: an immune response must cover diverse malignant cells without destroying essential host tissue. Their full scope was not established by the retained source text, so they remain qualified design constraints here rather than fully documented findings from that review. A convincing solution would need evidence that improved recognition does not merely exchange escape for unacceptable normal-tissue injury.

current_state.text: A Nature Reviews Immunology review published online in October 2025 and assigned to a March 2026 issue describes solid-tumor CAR-T efficacy as substantially constrained by the tumor microenvironment. Its retained abstract supports the trafficking, matrix, cellular suppression, checkpoint, and metabolic barriers described above. Access was limited to a subscription preview containing the abstract and references; the full review was not available to the supplied evidence review. Reference titles alone do not verify the outcomes of the underlying studies.

A BioWorld lede dated 23 June 2026 reports that China’s regulator approved satri-cel, also called CT-041, an autologous CLDN18.2-targeted CAR-T product. The reported indication is CLDN18.2-positive, HER2-negative advanced gastric or gastroesophageal junction adenocarcinoma after failure of at least two prior lines of therapy. The retained material contains the lede, while the article body was inaccessible. This establishes the existence and content of the trade report; it does not independently confirm the regulatory decision or supply efficacy data. The antigen-selected indication also cannot establish broad clearance across metastatic carcinomas.

The research notes describe a 2025 SSRN systematic-review preprint pooling 46 studies and 602 patients through 1 April 2025, with an estimated objective response rate of 9% and a 95% confidence interval of 5–14%. No source text was retained for this citation, so the supplied evidence review could not verify the counts, search cutoff, estimate, or publication status. These figures are preserved as an unverified report from the research, not an established pooled benchmark. Objective response is also a different outcome from durable, treatment-free complete clearance.

The research also attributes to a Lancet article dated 7 June 2025 a randomized satri-cel trial in previously treated gastric or gastroesophageal junction cancer. It reports median progression-free survival of 3.25 months with satri-cel versus 1.77 months with the comparator, with a hazard ratio of 0.37 and a 95% confidence interval of 0.24–0.56. The description of this as the first randomized solid-tumor CAR-T trial, along with the numerical results, could not be verified because no source text was retained. If accurate, those results would demonstrate a progression-free-survival benefit in the studied setting; they would not establish sterilizing clearance or the proportion achieving lasting complete responses.

A June 2025 Cancers review is described in the research as distinguishing immunotherapy progress in microsatellite-instability colorectal cancer from unconvincing results in microsatellite-stable colorectal cancer. A June 2026 Hematological Oncology review is cited for continuing solid-tumor CAR-T limitations. Neither citation has retained source text, so the supplied evidence review could not verify the former’s exact conclusion or the latter’s findings. These citations therefore provide qualified research context rather than independently established clinical summaries.

Evidence boundary: the research’s broader claim that checkpoint blockade and cell therapy already cure or durably control a minority of patients with melanoma, some lymphomas, and selected mismatch-repair-deficient tumors was not established by the retained clinical text. The supplied evidence supports important resistance mechanisms and an attributed approval report, while leaving several efficacy claims unverified. It does not demonstrate the proposed sterilizing capability. Because the freshness record is empty, it also cannot establish a complete clinical baseline or prove that the capability remained broadly unavailable as of 1 November 2026. Missing evidence does not show that the reported results are false.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed clinical demonstration: a prespecified trial in metastatic microsatellite-stable colorectal, pancreatic, or prostate cancer would show independently confirmed complete responses in a majority of all enrolled patients, sustained for a prespecified multiyear period after treatment stops. The protocol should define eligibility, the response assessment, when treatment ends, how subsequent anticancer treatment affects the endpoint, and how missing follow-up is handled. The majority threshold and multiyear requirement are proposed benchmarks for this concept, not established clinical standards.
completion_criteria.label: Confirmed multiyear treatment-free complete responses in most enrolled patients

completion_criteria.text: Proposed safety and reproducibility requirements: durable responses should occur without destruction of vital normal tissue and within prospectively defined acceptable limits for serious, persistent, and delayed toxicity. Independent replication and consistent results across centers would strengthen the case. Broader claims would require representative populations and separate evidence across cancer types, antigen profiles, disease burdens, and metastatic sites. A finite set of successful trials would establish demonstrated breadth within those boundaries, not literal universality.
completion_criteria.label: Durable responses preserve vital tissues within prespecified acceptable toxicity limits

completion_criteria.text: Proposed interpretation: long-term treatment-free complete responses, supported by complementary assessments for residual disease and continued relapse surveillance, would provide convincing evidence of durable clinical clearance. No finite negative testing program could alone prove the absence of every viable malignant cell. Follow-up would need to distinguish persistent remission from delayed recurrence, with deaths and subsequent treatments accounted for. Improvements in response rate or gains of months in progression-free survival would remain valuable intermediate achievements rather than completion of this target.
completion_criteria.label: Clinical clearance supported by residual-disease assessments and continued relapse surveillance

related_concepts.text: Conceptual mapping from the supplied roster: ONC-03, “Eradication of dormant disseminated tumor cells that cause late relapse,” addresses reservoirs that may remain after visible disease clears. ONC-05, “Therapies that drive the whole clonal population to extinction,” overlaps directly with preventing antigen escape and eliminating resistant malignant subpopulations. ONC-02 specifies immune rejection of established metastatic carcinoma; ONC-03 emphasizes dormant disease, while ONC-05 emphasizes extinction across the clonal population without specifying an immune mechanism. These objectives reinforce one another but should remain distinct.

Conceptual mapping: ONC-04, “A shared malignant dependency that renewing normal tissues can spare,” concerns selective vulnerability and could help address the safety problem of distinguishing cancer from essential normal tissue. It does not itself establish immune rejection. ONC-07, “Body-wide delivery that alters essentially every malignant cell,” overlaps with reaching disseminated disease, but direct alteration of essentially every cancer cell is a different requirement from enabling an immune system to clear tumor deposits.

Conceptual mapping: ONC-12, “Off-the-shelf cell therapy that matches autologous cures and can be given at ordinary scale,” addresses availability, manufacturing, and deployment of cell therapy. ONC-02 could in principle be demonstrated with an individualized product before those access problems are solved. Conversely, scalable cell manufacture would not establish effective clearance of resistant carcinomas. ONC-06, “Stable reversion of carcinoma cells to non-malignant tissue identity,” proposes changing malignant cell identity rather than eliminating the cells through immune rejection.

Conceptual mapping: ONC-01, “Mortality-reducing detection of lethal cancers while they are still localized,” and ONC-10, “A reliable distinction between early neoplasms that will kill and those that will not,” concern detection and risk discrimination before established metastatic disease. ONC-08, “Interception of non-viral precancers before they invade,” and ONC-09, “Prophylactic immunity that prevents the common non-viral cancers,” concern prevention or interception. ONC-09 shares an immune theme with ONC-02, but preventing cancer and clearing bulky existing metastases require different demonstrations.

Conceptual mapping: ONC-11, “Real-time, cell-resolution guidance that makes incomplete cancer surgery uncommon,” concerns local operative completeness. Better surgery could complement systemic immune treatment, but does not by itself demonstrate clearance of disseminated disease. These distinctions use the supplied roster titles; fuller definitions were not provided, so the mappings should not be read as verified boundaries of complete specifications.

unresolved_issues: The SSRN pooled estimates, search cutoff, and preprint/publication status remain unverified because no source text was retained.
The satri-cel randomized-trial efficacy figures and priority claim remain unverified from the supplied evidence.
The Chinese regulatory decision is represented by a partial trade report rather than independent regulatory documentation.
The MSS colorectal review conclusion, Wiley review findings, and broader named-cancer cure or durable-control baseline lack retained supporting text.
The retained abstract does not establish the full scope of antigen heterogeneity, antigen loss, or normal-tissue injury from shared targets.
The empty freshness record prevents establishing comprehensive coverage through 1 November 2026 or a definitive present-day absence of the proposed capability.
The proposed follow-up duration, acceptable toxicity limits, residual-disease assessments, and replication design still require operational specification.
The roster provides titles rather than full concept definitions, so cross-concept boundaries remain provisional.

The review’s suggested replacement current-state text omitted unverified quantitative claims. That omission was not adopted because the task explicitly requests preservation of unresolved quantitative detail; the figures are instead retained with clear attribution and limitations.

brief.title: Lasting immune clearance of cancer that has spread
possible: People with large cancers that have spread could finish treatment and stay cancer-free. A controllable immune treatment would eliminate the original tumour and growing tumours elsewhere while preserving vital healthy tissues.
The goal includes difficult pancreatic, colorectal, prostate and breast cancers. It requires reaching cancer cells across different sites and eliminating every population capable of growing back.
why: For patients who respond, lasting clearance would reduce dependence on repeated treatment and prolonged efforts to keep cancer under control.
Reliable clearance in most patients with these cancers would give doctors a way to achieve lasting remission across substantial, widespread disease.

sources.quote: The median survival time among patients living with metastases is 10 months
sources.cited_for: The study illustrates the burden of metastatic cancer.
sources.not_established: The pooled survival estimate does not establish outcomes for each target cancer or the benefit of a future treatment.

shown: Carsgen’s satri-cel has reportedly reached Chinese approval for selected advanced stomach cancers. It uses a patient’s engineered immune cells. This is the clearest reported clinical advance toward the goal.
missing: Immune cells must reach large tumours and growing deposits throughout the body, then remain active despite local suppression.
Treatment must eliminate diverse cancer-cell populations while preserving vital healthy tissues.
Trials must demonstrate lasting complete clearance in most enrolled patients after treatment ends.

milestones.label: Most patients remain cancer-free for years after treatment
milestones.explanation: A trial in eligible colorectal, pancreatic or prostate cancer would have to confirm complete responses in most enrolled patients for years after treatment ends. This would establish durable benefit in the tested population.

milestones.label: Lasting responses preserve vital tissues within acceptable toxicity limits
milestones.explanation: Durable responses would have to preserve vital tissues and meet predefined limits on serious and lasting harm, with consistent results across centres. This would establish safety and reproducibility.

milestones.label: Disease testing and follow-up support lasting clearance
milestones.explanation: Complementary tests for remaining cancer and continued monitoring for relapse would have to support long-term, treatment-free complete responses. This would strengthen the case for durable clinical clearance.

uncertain: No finite set of negative tests can prove that every cancer cell capable of regrowth has disappeared.
The required follow-up duration, acceptable toxicity limits and tests for remaining disease still need definition.
How broadly success would extend across cancer types, tumour burdens and sites of spread remains open.

page.title: Treatment-free complete remission of metastatic carcinomas
page.definition: Immune treatment clears detectable established carcinomas, cancers originating in epithelial tissue, and their growing metastases, and complete remission persists after treatment ends. Clinical remission cannot establish that every viable malignant cell has disappeared.

goal.need: In a US SEER cohort of 1,030,937 people newly diagnosed with metastatic cancer during 1992–2019, median survival was 10 months. This historical estimate pools cancer types and does not describe current prognosis in each carcinoma case. The target is clearance that persists after treatment ends, rather than a temporary reduction in tumour size.

statements.quote: SITC aims to make cancer immunotherapy a standard of care and the word “cure” a reality for cancer patients everywhere.
the approach needs to be further refined and tested in more types of solid cancers.
statements.context: Steven A. Rosenberg, discussing personalised cellular immunotherapy for metastatic colorectal cancer.

completion.title: Five-year treatment-free complete remissions are independently reproduced in all four carcinoma cases.
completion.criterion: In each listed case, at least two independently conducted prospective studies demonstrate confirmed complete responses to finite immune treatment in patients with measurable metastatic disease. Responders remain alive in complete remission, without further anticancer treatment, for at least 5 years after the later of response confirmation and treatment completion. Responses use RECIST 1.1 plus disease-specific assessments where needed; treatment meets the studies’ prespecified safety limits. This is an operational test of replicated clinical remission, not proof of sterilizing eradication.
completion.set_by: Atlas operational criterion; no outside body’s validated completion test was located.
completion.basis: Searches of FDA oncology endpoint guidance, RECIST, NCI cure definitions, SITC goals and trial registries found no validated cross-carcinoma test for sterilizing eradication or a required cure fraction. The Atlas therefore combines published response criteria and NCI’s qualified five-year remission convention with independent replication in each case. No majority-response threshold is imposed. Late relapse remains possible.

milestones.title: Preclinical studies establish biological activity and a starting dose for a carcinoma immune treatment.
milestones.criterion: For a cellular immune treatment, preclinical studies establish biological plausibility, biologically active dose levels, and feasibility and reasonable safety for clinical administration. FDA specifies no universal tumour-regression percentage. In a study published on 16 October 2017, PSCA-targeted CAR T cells, immune cells engineered to recognise a prostate-associated antigen, caused regression of established prostate-cancer xenografts of approximately 500 mm³ in mice; the intravenous-treatment experiment used 3 mice per group.
milestones.set_by: FDA, Preclinical Assessment of Investigational Cellular and Gene Therapy Products, section III.A; nonbinding recommendations for the cellular-therapy route.

milestones.title: An immune treatment reaches a patient with metastatic carcinoma in an authorised clinical study.
milestones.criterion: At least one patient with metastatic carcinoma receives the investigational immune treatment in a regulator-permitted, ethics-approved clinical study evaluating administration and adverse reactions. A phase 1 prostate-cancer study published on 12 June 2024 treated 14 men with PSCA-targeted CAR T cells after FDA investigational-new-drug and institutional review board approval. Grade 1–2 cytokine-release syndrome occurred in 5 of 14 patients; grade 3 cystitis was dose limiting.
milestones.set_by: FDA, Considerations for the Design of Early-Phase Clinical Trials of Cellular and Gene Therapy Products, introduction and section IV.A.
milestones.threshold_quote: initial introduction of an investigational new drug into humans

milestones.title: An immune treatment reduces a metastatic carcinoma’s target-lesion diameter sum by at least 30%.
milestones.criterion: RECIST 1.1 partial response requires at least a 30% decrease from baseline in the sum of target-lesion diameters, without new lesions or non-target progression. Confirmation is required when response is the primary endpoint in a non-randomised study. A pancreatic-cancer case published on 2 June 2022 had a 72% partial response, ongoing at 6 months. NCI reported responses lasting 4–7 months in 3 of 7 colorectal-cancer patients on 11 July 2024; its release does not specify their molecular subtype.
milestones.set_by: RECIST Working Group, revised RECIST guideline version 1.1, sections 4.3–4.6.
milestones.threshold_quote: At least a 30% decrease in the sum of diameters of target lesions

milestones.title: An immune treatment produces complete disappearance of detectable metastatic carcinoma.
milestones.criterion: RECIST 1.1 complete response requires disappearance of target and non-target lesions, pathological lymph nodes below 10 mm in short axis, normalisation of applicable tumour markers, and no new lesions. Confirmation follows the protocol when required. A report published on 4 June 2018 described complete regression in one patient with hormone receptor-positive metastatic breast cancer after tumour-infiltrating lymphocytes, interleukin-2 and pembrolizumab; that study used RECIST 1.0.
milestones.set_by: RECIST Working Group, revised RECIST guideline version 1.1, sections 4.3–4.6 and table 1.

milestones.title: A patient remains in complete remission from metastatic carcinoma for at least 5 years.
milestones.criterion: Complete remission continues for at least 5 years. NCI describes this as a convention used by some doctors, while warning that recurrence can occur later. A breast-cancer pilot report published on 1 February 2022 described one complete response among 6 treated patients, ongoing at 66 months. The earlier report placed full lesion resolution 1 year after cell infusion; these reports alone do not establish 5 years measured from confirmed complete response.
milestones.set_by: Clinical convention described by NCI in Understanding Cancer Prognosis; this is not a validated criterion for sterilizing cure.
milestones.threshold_quote: If you remain in complete remission for 5 years or more, some doctors may say that you are cured.

not_found: No validated clinical test establishing elimination of every viable malignant cell across these carcinomas was located.
No uniform acceptable-toxicity limit or required complete-response fraction was located for this capability.
The full 2024 colorectal T-cell paper could not be opened; the clinical figures are attributed to NCI’s account of the published study.
The molecular subtype of that seven-patient colorectal cohort could not be verified from the opened clinical text.
No peer-reviewed update establishing five years measured from confirmed complete response was located for the cited breast-cancer responder.
Independent prospective replication of five-year treatment-free complete remission in every listed case was not located.

results.detail: The study reports dose-dependent tumor control and no obvious tissue damage, with lower graft-versus-host disease and cytokine-release findings than CAR-αβ cells. Scalable production in clinically relevant quantities remains a challenge.
results.quote: Furthermore, administration of a high dose (6×10⁶ PSCA CAR-Vδ1 T cells per infusion, delivered every other week for a total of three infusions, with each dose divided between intraperitoneal (i.p.) and intravenous routes for experimental and control groups) significantly extended the survival of treated mice

results.detail: The active regimen used 5 million murine CAR T cells after cyclophosphamide preconditioning. No overt toxicity or gross changes in normal PSCA-expressing tissues were observed in the treated mice. The model may not fully represent human PSCA expression.
